sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emili.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about El Salvador.
El Salvador is a small, tropical,
and friendly country in Central America.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is El Salvador?
El Salvador is in Central America.
It is between Honduras and Guatemala.
To the south, it touches the Pacific Ocean.
It is the smallest country in Central America,
but it has many beautiful places.
What is the capital city of El Salvador?
The capital city is San Salvador.
It is a busy city with mountains, museums, and markets.
It is the political, cultural, and economic center of the country.
Other cities include Santa Ana,
San Miguel La Libertad, famous for its beaches.
How many people live in El Salvador?
About six, five million people live in El Salvador.
Most people live in cities,
but many also live in small towns and villages.
El Salvador is known for its hard-working people
and strong communities.
What language do people speak in El Salvador?
People speak Spanish.
It is the official language.
Some indigenous words are also used in daily life.
In tourist areas, some people speak a little English.
What is the weather like in El Salvador?
El Salvador has a tropical climate.
It is usually warm or hot.
There are two seasons,
the dry season from November to April,
the rainy season from May to October.
It rains a lot in the rainy season,
but the country stays very green.
What does El Salvador look like?
El Salvador has volcanoes and mountains,
lakes and rivers, rainforests and farmland,
long beaches along the Pacific Ocean.
It is called the land of volcanoes because it has many.
What animals live in El Salvador?
In El Salvador, you can see parrots, iguanas and toucans,
monkeys, deer and armadillos,
frogs, lizards and turtles.
In the countryside, people keep chickens,
dogs, cats and cows.
What do people eat in El Salvador?
Salvador and food is simple, tasty and often homemade.
The most famous food is the pupusa,
a thick corn tortilla filled with cheese,
beans or meat.
It is eaten with curtito,
pickled cabbage and salsa.
Other popular foods include tamales,
corn dough wrapped in leaves,
yuca frita, fried cassava,
empanadas, sweet or savory pastries,
rice and beans, eggs and plantains.
What do people drink in El Salvador?
People drink coffee.
El Salvador grows very good coffee.
Porchata, a sweet drink made from seeds and spices,
juices like mango, tamarind or pineapple,
milk, tea and water.
Cold drinks are popular because the weather is warm.
What is life like in El Salvador?
Life in El Salvador is family-centered and community-based.
People enjoy spending time with family,
cooking and eating together,
going to church, playing soccer, football,
listening to music and dancing,
markets, street food and festivals are part of daily life.
What are some holidays and traditions in El Salvador?
Independence Day,
September 15th,
Holy Week,
Samana Santa before Easter,
Christmas and New Years with fireworks and big dinners.
Day of the Cross, May 3rd with flowers and trees.
Fiesta's Patranalas,
town festivals with parades, music and food.
People celebrate with music, dancing and traditional clothes.
Some fun facts about El Salvador.
The currency is the U.S. dollar.
The flag is blue and white with a triangle and five volcanoes.
El Salvador has over 20 volcanoes.
It is famous for surfing.
The waves are perfect.
The word El Salvador means the Savior in Spanish.
Now you know many things about El Salvador.
You know where it is, what people speak and what they eat.
You learned about the weather, traditions and daily life.
Great job.
I am Emili.
Goodbye or as they say in Spanish, Adios.
